checks.location: Corollary 4.1 (Sec. 4) and proof A.8, first term of round bound; also wall-clock bound first term
checks.claim: R >= c_R(Delta L sigma^2/(n eps Hbar) + ...) rounds suffice for E||grad f(xbar^rhat)||^2 <= eps; wall-clock leading term Delta L sigma^2 tau_H/(n eps).
checks.explanation: The first term loses a factor of inverse accuracy when the proof substitutes its step size into the optimization term. The same error appears in the wall-clock bound.
checks.demonstration:
The preceding theorem has terms $4\Delta/(\eta\bar H R)$ and $4L\eta\sigma^2/n$. Choosing $\eta$ of order $n\varepsilon/(L\sigma^2)$ therefore requires a stochastic round term of order $\Delta L\sigma^2/(n\bar H\varepsilon^2)$.

An example also rules out the stronger printed rate under the global moment assumptions. Use one worker, one coordinate, full synchronization, one local step, unit computation time and zero communication delay, so $\bar H=H_{\max}=1$ and $X=0$. Set
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2/2,&|x|\le1,\\|x|-1/2,&|x|>1,\end{cases}\qquad g(x,\xi)=\operatorname{clip}(x,-1,1)+\xi,
\]
with independent equiprobable signs $\xi=\pm1$. This is a lower-bounded, differentiable, globally $1$-smooth objective; the estimator is unbiased, has variance one, and has global second moment at most two. Starting at $x_0=1$, every allowed constant step $0<\eta\le1/8$ keeps the iterates in $[-1,1]$. With $a=\eta/(2-\eta)$, their average squared gradient is exactly
\[
A_R=a+(1-a)\frac{1-(1-\eta)^{2R}}{R(2\eta-\eta^2)}.
\]
If $\eta R\ge1$, then $A_R\ge\eta/2$ and $A_R>0.4/(\eta R)$, hence $A_R\ge\sqrt{0.2/R}$. If $\eta R<1$, then $A_R\ge e^{-16/7}$. Thus $R=\lceil C/\varepsilon\rceil$ fails to attain accuracy $\varepsilon$ for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, for every fixed $C$ and every allowed constant step. The printed bound has exactly that order in this instance.
checks.repair: Replace the first round term by $\Delta L\sigma^2/(n\varepsilon^2\bar H)$ and the first time term by $\Delta L\sigma^2\tau_H/(n\varepsilon^2)$, where $\tau_H$ is the harmonic mean of worker computation times. The other terms keep their powers. The proof’s existing step-size choice and the preceding theorem then give the corrected rate by allocating a constant fraction of the error budget to each term.
checks.scope: This corrects the conversion from the displayed convergence bound to round and time complexity. It does not certify every preceding theorem. The following minibatch discussion already prints the squared accuracy denominator.
checks.claimContext: Corollary 4.1 bounds the rounds needed for $\mathbb E\|\nabla f(\bar x^{\hat r})\|^2\le\varepsilon$, with $\hat r$ uniform over the rounds. Here $\Delta=f(x^0)-f^\star$, $n$ is the number of workers, $\bar H$ is their average local-step count, $L$ is the smoothness constant, and $\sigma^2$ bounds stochastic-gradient variance.
